title: The Voice of the Silence
author: H. P. Blavatsky
description: The Voice of the Silence, being chosen fragments from the 'Book of the Golden Precepts', for the daily use of lanoos (disciples), translated and annotated by H. P. B. (H. P. Blavatsky) (London and New York, 1889). Blavatsky presented the work as translated from a secret Tibetan text she had memorised, studied in the same school as the Stanzas of Dzyan. It consists of three 'fragments': The Voice of the Silence, on the stilling of the senses and the mind so the disciple can hear the inner voice and achieve union with the Self; The Two Paths, contrasting the 'Doctrine of the Eye' (personal liberation) with the 'Doctrine of the Heart', the path of compassion of one who renounces nirvana to help humanity; and The Seven Portals, on the six paramitas or virtues and the seventh portal of wisdom. It was endorsed by the Dalai Lama in a 1989 centenary edition and is one of the most devotional texts of Theosophy.
